text:
sam: Quick heads-up — ran the staging load profile for the coalesce/jitter tweak we rolled yesterday. Seeing a noticeable p95 regression and KV hit-rate drop. Putting raw snippets below, want quick eyes before I start tuning.
maria-ml: Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 and the kernel switch trace? Also the exact coalesce/jitter params used in the rollout.
sam: sure — from the 15m run (tail of steady-state):
```
p50: 22ms
p95: 145ms
p99: 310ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.41  # before -> after
effective_batch_tokens_p50: 96 -> 52
kernel_select_log (sample):
  2026-03-17T18:02:12Z select: attention_opt_v2 (batch_tokens=128)
  2026-03-17T18:02:13Z select: attention_generic (batch_tokens=40)
  2026-03-17T18:02:14Z select: attention_generic (batch_tokens=28)
config changed: coalesce_delay_ms: 3 -> 8; jitter_ms: 0 -> 4; microbatch_interval_us: 800 -> 1200
```
kevin: ouch. That coalesce_delay+jitter combo could be fragmenting workloads so batches are smaller and kernel selector falls back to the generic path. Do you have the batch size distribution?
sam: batch_size_dist snapshot (percent of requests): {"1": 0.21, "2": 0.33, "4": 0.28, "8+": 0.18}
lia: looks like we lost a healthy tail of 8+ batchings. My bet is twofold: (1) jitter stretched windows so frequent prefix misses -> KV priming doesn't amortize, and (2) smaller batches push token-count below kernel thresholds. Suggest adding a small min_coalesce to let prefixes accumulate.
maria-ml: agreed. propose a short A/B experiment: baseline vs conservative window. config snippet for experiment:
```
experiment: {
  name: "coalesce-jitter-conservative",
  min_coalesce_ms: 6,
  target_coalesce_ms: 6,
  max_jitter_ms: 2,
  microbatch_interval_us: 1000,
  token_budget_target: 1024,
  queue_policy: "age_weighted"
}
```
Goal: restore effective batch_tokens p50 ~90 and kv_hit >= 0.6 while keeping mean latency within 10%.
sam: I'll kick that off now (canary 5% staging -> 20% later). Ramp plan: 5m ramp, 15m steady, compare p50/p95/kv-hit and kernel_switch_events. Anyone object?
toni: no objection. Add a dashboard tile for kernel_switch_events/min and KV priming latency. If the kernel switch rate is the biggest delta we can consider a short-term guard to prefer attention_opt_v2 for seq<=32 when batch_tokens>=64.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started: coalesce-jitter-conservative -> staging (5% nodes) :rocket:
kevin: if the experiment doesn't help, another mitigation is policy-level token-budget uplift so the selector sees higher token counts (even if that increases small-op cost). But let's try the min_coalesce first.
maria-ml: agreed — and instrument a histogram 'batch_tokens_before_kernel_select' so we can correlate kernel decisions with batch tokens quickly.
sam: uploaded a raw trace to the run bundle: https://internal.grafana/redwood/d/xyz123/coalesce-experiments (dash + raw traces). I'll post results after the steady window. thanks all.
kevin: one more: add an alert if kv_cache_hit_rate drops >15% from baseline during rollouts, so we don't silently degrade throughput on other customers.
lia: noted — I'll add that alert to the coalesce alerting group.
sam: nice fast sync — will report back in ~40m with numbers.
